title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Risk-on week; energy ripped, tech lagged, small-caps held.  
The week’s arc was a grind higher into Thursday’s record close on cooler CPI, then a Friday stall on soft retail sales and geopolitics. Energy led decisively (XLE +7.67%), while cyclical consumer and materials lagged, and VIX fell to 14.2. Dominant driver: rotation out of mega-cap tech into energy, storage, and defensives.

INDICES — SPY +0.40%, QQQ +1.11%, IWM +1.17%, DIA -0.52%. Small > large by 0.06pp (IWM +1.17% vs QQQ +1.11%). VIX fell to 14.2, below its 20-day 16.6. Most notable cross-asset move: silver +1.70% WTD, 20d +15.16%. No index below its 200-day MA.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLE Energy +7.67%, XLU Utilities +1.61%, XLC Comm +1.53%, XLP Staples +1.14%, XLK Tech +1.09%, XLV Health +1.02%, XLF Financials +0.97%, XLI Industrials +0.72%, XLRE Real Estate +0.64%, XLB Materials -0.61%, XLY Discretionary -1.38%. Top industries: DRAM +13.28%, OIH +8.51%, XOP +8.47%, USO +7.31%. Bottom: JETS -3.01%, IBIT -3.18%, FXI -3.54%, KWEB -5.76%. Money flowed into energy and storage/memory (Seagate +11% Friday); out of China, airlines, and crypto. Rotation state: AI hardware fading / high-to-low rotation.

DRIVERS — The week’s arc: CPI in line Tuesday lifted futures; Thursday’s record close on cooler inflation; Friday broke it on July retail sales -0.6% m/m and UMich sentiment at 51.0, while Brent +0.7% to ~$87.7 on Strait of Hormuz naval blockade headlines lifted XLE +1.5%. Semis unwound Friday: XLK -0.6%, SMH -0.8%, AVGO -5.9%, AMAT ~-5-7%; healthcare XLV -0.5% on Lilly, Veeva, Vertex. VIX fell despite Friday’s dip; volume was thin overall (indices avg 0.62x). No Fed decision this week; next FOMC Sep 16.

WHAT'S NEXT — Watch extension in energy (OVX 49.5, XLE 20d +7.33%) and whether DRAM’s +13.28% leadership broadens into chips. VIX at 14.2 with SPY ATM IV 6.6% suggests complacency ahead of Sep 16 FOMC, where hikes are 32.7% priced. Small-cap breadth (IWM above GEX flip 305) and defensive bid in XLU/XLP could confirm high-to-low rotation.
